candidates.summary: chromeShot runs Chrome with no deadline, and --virtual-time-budget does not bound the process
candidates.failure_scenario: A pull request adds or edits a realm whose markdown embeds an external image, `![](http://slow.example/x.png)`. gnoweb's image policy (AllowSvgDataImage) rejects only non-svg data: URIs and Crawler.mapURL leaves external URLs alone, so the snapshot page keeps that . ScreenshotPairs calls chromeShot on that page; the host accepts the connection and never answers, virtual time stops advancing, and Chrome never exits. exec.Command carries no context, so chromeShot blocks forever. pr-preview.yml sets no timeout-minutes, so the job holds a runner until GitHub's 360-minute default kills it, on every push, from any fork.
candidates.verify_by: cp reviews/.../tests/b4-reach-chromeshot-hang_test.go misc/gnopreview/ && cd misc/gnopreview && go test -run TestChromeShot -v -timeout 5m .  — control returns in <1s, the stalled-subresource case is still running at 60s
candidates.evidence: TestChromeShotPlainPage: "control returned in 810.479116ms" PASS. TestChromeShotStalledSubresource: "chromeShot still running after 1m0s" FAIL (60.00s). Raw chromium probe with the exact flag set: plain rc=0, stalled page rc=124 under `timeout 90` and no PNG written. grep for timeout-minutes in .github/workflows/pr-preview.yml: no hit.

candidates.summary: Screenshot is unreachable for a PR touching gnoweb and a realm, so the comment prints the gnoweb lead-in over an empty grid
candidates.failure_scenario: A PR that edits gnoweb and a realm has plan.Gnoweb true and len(plan.ChangedRealms) > 0. main.go's `if len(plan.ChangedRealms) > 0 { Pairs } else if plan.Gnoweb { Shots }` takes the first arm, so plan.Shots stays nil even though the four shotPlan pages were crawled (plan.go:37-40 seeds them). comment.go:47-53 then writes "This PR changes **gnoweb** and realm sources." followed by shotGrid(nil) — an empty string — so the reviewer is told gnoweb changed and shown no sample rendering.
candidates.verify_by: go test ./misc/gnopreview -run TestComment with a Plan{Gnoweb: true, ChangedRealms: ["gno.land/r/x/leaf"], Shots: nil}: expect the gnoweb sample images, observe the sentence with nothing under it

candidates.summary: a failed before-shot is published as a lone after image, indistinguishable from a realm that is new
candidates.failure_scenario: renderBase returns nil on any base-render failure, or chromeShot fails on the before page alone (shots.go:90-95). pair.Before stays "" while pair.New is false, and comment.go:106-113 attaches the explaining note only when New is true. The PR comment then shows one image with no caption, and the reader reads a realm that exists at the merge base as having no before state.
candidates.verify_by: go test ./misc/gnopreview -run TestCommentPairs with ShotPair{Realm: "gno.land/r/x/leaf", After: "_shots/a.png", Before: "", New: false}: expect a note saying the before shot failed, observe a bare

candidates.summary: findChrome silently ignores an explicit -chrome path that does not resolve
candidates.failure_scenario: `gnopreview render -chrome /opt/chrom/chrome` (a typo, or a path absent from the runner image) falls through LookPath and Stat and the loop continues to google-chrome, chromium and the macOS bundle. The run screenshots with a browser the operator did not name and says nothing; the pinned-browser intent of the flag is lost, and a version-specific rendering difference is invisible.
candidates.verify_by: read shots.go:195-213: the explicit candidate is one entry of the same slice as the fallbacks, with no error path when it fails both LookPath and Stat

candidates.summary: the viewport-only 1280x860 shot can make before and after identical while the diff sits below the fold
candidates.failure_scenario: Chrome's --screenshot with --window-size=1280,860 captures the viewport, not the full page. A realm whose Render output changes below 860px produces two byte-similar images, and pairGrid presents them as "before — merge base" and "after — this PR": the comment asserts a comparison that shows none of the change.
candidates.verify_by: run chromeShot over a fixture page whose only difference is at y=1200 and compare the two PNGs; expect a visible delta, observe none

candidates.summary: serve returns the listener as the Closer, so the http.Server is never shut down
candidates.failure_scenario: Screenshot and ScreenshotPairs defer srv.Close() on the net.Listener. Serve returns, but the http.Server keeps its connections: Chrome's keep-alive connection to the snapshot server is neither drained nor closed, and the handler goroutine lives until the process exits. The //nolint comment on line 162 covers Serve's return and not the server's connections.
candidates.verify_by: read shots.go:153-163: srv is an *http.Server, the returned io.Closer is ln, and nothing calls srv.Close or srv.Shutdown

candidates.summary: Screenshot reaches into c.pages while ScreenshotPairs uses the FileOf accessor
candidates.failure_scenario: Two canonicalization paths for the same lookup: Screenshot does c.pages[canonicalURL(s.url)] directly, ScreenshotPairs calls head.FileOf. A later change to FileOf's key handling — a trailing-slash rule, a case fold — fixes one caller and leaves the other silently missing its pages, and a missing page here is a `continue` with no message.
candidates.verify_by: grep -n 'c.pages\[' misc/gnopreview/*.go: Screenshot is the only caller outside crawl.go that indexes the map instead of calling FileOf
